questions.question: What is the immediate product formed when an organic molecule (M) is bombarded by a 70 eV electron beam in mass spectrometry?

options.label: A
options.text: A neutral radical and a hydride anion.

options.label: B
options.text: A high-energy radical cation (molecular ion, M⁺•) formed by ejection of a single valence electron from the molecule: M + e⁻ → M⁺• + 2e⁻.

options.label: C
options.text: A carbanion formed by electron capture.

options.label: D
options.text: A doubly charged dication [M²⁺].

questions.correct_answer: A high-energy radical cation (molecular ion, M⁺•) formed by ejection of a single valence electron from the molecule: M + e⁻ → M⁺• + 2e⁻.
questions.explanation: High-energy electron impact ejects an electron from the lowest ionization energy orbital, generating the molecular radical cation (M⁺•).

questions.question: What is the driving force and curved-arrow flow during the α-cleavage of a 2-butanol radical cation?

options.label: A
options.text: Heterolytic cleavage of the C-O bond to form a hydroxyl cation.

options.label: B
options.text: Expulsion of methane gas.

options.label: C
options.text: Homolytic cleavage of the C-C bond adjacent to the oxygen radical cation, expelling a neutral ethyl radical and forming a resonance-stabilized oxonium ion (m/z 45).

options.label: D
options.text: Loss of water to form a butadiene radical.

questions.correct_answer: Homolytic cleavage of the C-C bond adjacent to the oxygen radical cation, expelling a neutral ethyl radical and forming a resonance-stabilized oxonium ion (m/z 45).
questions.explanation: Alpha-cleavage is driven by formation of an exceptionally stable, resonance-stabilized oxonium cation [CH₃CH=OH⁺].

questions.question: What structural requirement and transition state geometry are essential for a McLafferty rearrangement in mass spectrometry?

options.label: A
options.text: An alcohol with an α-hydrogen undergoing a 3-membered ring flip.

options.label: B
options.text: An aromatic ring with ortho substituents.

options.label: C
options.text: A tertiary halide undergoing unimolecular ionization.

options.label: D
options.text: A carbonyl compound with a γ-hydrogen atom undergoing a six-membered cyclic transition state to transfer the γ-H to oxygen with elimination of a neutral alkene.

questions.correct_answer: A carbonyl compound with a γ-hydrogen atom undergoing a six-membered cyclic transition state to transfer the γ-H to oxygen with elimination of a neutral alkene.
questions.explanation: The McLafferty rearrangement requires a γ-hydrogen that transfers to the radical cation oxygen through a 6-membered cyclic transition state.

questions.question: Why do alkylbenzenes (e.g., toluene, propylbenzene) characteristically show a base peak at m/z 91 in mass spectrometry?

options.label: A
options.text: Toluene fragments into three acetylene molecules.

options.label: B
options.text: The benzene ring expels a methyl radical directly.

options.label: C
options.text: Benzylic cleavage generates the benzyl cation (PhCH₂⁺), which rapidly rearranges to the aromatic, resonance-stabilized cycloheptatrienyl (tropylium) cation.

options.label: D
options.text: The phenyl cation coordinates with nitrogen gas.

questions.correct_answer: Benzylic cleavage generates the benzyl cation (PhCH₂⁺), which rapidly rearranges to the aromatic, resonance-stabilized cycloheptatrienyl (tropylium) cation.
questions.explanation: The m/z 91 benzyl cation rearranges into the symmetrical, aromatic 6π tropylium cation (C₇H₇⁺).

questions.question: What is the physical reason that an organic molecule with an odd number of nitrogen atoms has an odd nominal molecular weight?

options.label: A
options.text: Nitrogen has an even atomic mass (14 Da) but an odd valence (3 bonds), requiring an odd number of monovalent hydrogens compared to carbon and oxygen.

options.label: B
options.text: Nitrogen decays radioactively inside the mass spectrometer.

options.label: C
options.text: Nitrogen only forms ionic bonds in organic molecules.

options.label: D
options.text: Nitrogen contains an unpaired nuclear proton.

questions.correct_answer: Nitrogen has an even atomic mass (14 Da) but an odd valence (3 bonds), requiring an odd number of monovalent hydrogens compared to carbon and oxygen.
questions.explanation: Because nitrogen forms three bonds with an atomic weight of 14, molecules containing an odd number of nitrogens must contain an odd number of hydrogens.

questions.question: Why does a monochlorinated compound exhibit two molecular ion peaks separated by 2 m/z in a 3:1 intensity ratio?

options.label: A
options.text: Chlorine absorbs two extra electrons in 25% of molecules.

options.label: B
options.text: Chlorine exists naturally as two stable isotopes: ³⁵Cl (75.8% abundance) and ³⁷Cl (24.2% abundance), creating a 3:1 ratio of M⁺ to (M+2)⁺.

options.label: C
options.text: The molecule undergoes rapid hydrogen abstraction in the source.

options.label: D
options.text: Chlorine fragments into two chloride ions.

questions.correct_answer: Chlorine exists naturally as two stable isotopes: ³⁵Cl (75.8% abundance) and ³⁷Cl (24.2% abundance), creating a 3:1 ratio of M⁺ to (M+2)⁺.
questions.explanation: The natural ~3:1 ratio of ³⁵Cl to ³⁷Cl isotopes directly generates the diagnostic M / (M+2) isotopic fingerprint.

questions.question: What is the isotopic origin of the characteristic twin molecular ion peaks of equal height (1:1 ratio) in brominated compounds?

options.label: A
options.text: Bromine undergoes 50% homolytic cleavage during ionization.

options.label: B
options.text: Bromine exists as a dimer in mass spectrometers.

options.label: C
options.text: The molecular ion has two conformations in gas phase.

options.label: D
options.text: Bromine occurs in nature as two stable isotopes in nearly equal abundance: ⁷⁹Br (50.7%) and ⁸¹Br (49.3%), yielding equal M⁺ and (M+2)⁺ peak heights.

questions.correct_answer: Bromine occurs in nature as two stable isotopes in nearly equal abundance: ⁷⁹Br (50.7%) and ⁸¹Br (49.3%), yielding equal M⁺ and (M+2)⁺ peak heights.
questions.explanation: The nearly 1:1 natural abundance of ⁷⁹Br and ⁸¹Br creates the diagnostic twin peak pattern in mass spectrometry.

questions.question: Why is the C=C stretching vibration of symmetrical trans-2-butene inactive (invisible) in infrared spectroscopy?

options.label: A
options.text: Because the C=C bond is too strong to vibrate.

options.label: B
options.text: Because trans-2-butene does not absorb any energy.

options.label: C
options.text: Because symmetrical stretching of the centrosymmetric trans-alkene produces zero net change in molecular dipole moment (dμ/dr = 0).

options.label: D
options.text: Because infrared light only detects nitrogen and oxygen.

questions.correct_answer: Because symmetrical stretching of the centrosymmetric trans-alkene produces zero net change in molecular dipole moment (dμ/dr = 0).
questions.explanation: Infrared absorption requires a vibration that causes a net change in the molecular dipole moment; centrosymmetric vibrations are IR inactive.

questions.topic: Carbonyl IR Force Constant vs Conjugation
questions.question: Why does the C=O stretching frequency decrease from 1715 cm⁻¹ in cyclohexanone to 1685 cm⁻¹ in cyclohex-2-en-1-one?

options.label: A
options.text: Resonance delocalization of π electrons into the adjacent double bond gives the C=O bond more single-bond character, lowering the bond force constant (k).

options.label: B
options.text: Cyclohexenone undergoes rapid keto-enol tautomerism.

options.label: C
options.text: Conjugation destroys the carbonyl dipole moment.

options.label: D
options.text: Conjugation increases the reduced mass (μ) of the carbonyl atoms.

questions.correct_answer: Resonance delocalization of π electrons into the adjacent double bond gives the C=O bond more single-bond character, lowering the bond force constant (k).
questions.explanation: According to Hooke's Law (ν ∝ √(k/μ)), resonance delocalization reduces bond order/force constant k, shifting absorption to lower wavenumber.

questions.question: Why does the O-H stretch of carboxylic acids appear as an extremely broad band between 2500–3300 cm⁻¹?

options.label: A
options.text: Carboxylic acids absorb moisture from the air during testing.

options.label: B
options.text: Carboxylic acids undergo continuous radical homolysis.

options.label: C
options.text: Carboxylic acids form strong, stable hydrogen-bonded dimers in solution, creating a continuum of perturbed O-H bond lengths and vibrational frequencies.

options.label: D
options.text: The O-H bond is completely ionic in solution.

questions.correct_answer: Carboxylic acids form strong, stable hydrogen-bonded dimers in solution, creating a continuum of perturbed O-H bond lengths and vibrational frequencies.
questions.explanation: Intermolecular centrosymmetric dimerization creates strong hydrogen bonds that severely weaken and broaden the O-H stretching potential.

questions.question: What is the immediate product formed when an organic molecule (M) is bombarded by a 70 eV electron beam in mass spectrometry?

options.label: A
options.text: A carbanion formed by electron capture.

options.label: B
options.text: A doubly charged dication [M²⁺].

options.label: C
options.text: A high-energy radical cation (molecular ion, M⁺•) formed by ejection of a single valence electron from the molecule: M + e⁻ → M⁺• + 2e⁻.

options.label: D
options.text: A neutral radical and a hydride anion.

questions.correct_answer: A high-energy radical cation (molecular ion, M⁺•) formed by ejection of a single valence electron from the molecule: M + e⁻ → M⁺• + 2e⁻.
questions.explanation: High-energy electron impact ejects an electron from the lowest ionization energy orbital, generating the molecular radical cation (M⁺•).

questions.question: What is the driving force and curved-arrow flow during the α-cleavage of a 2-butanol radical cation?

questions.question: What is the physical reason that an organic molecule with an odd number of nitrogen atoms has an odd nominal molecular weight?

options.label: A
options.text: Nitrogen only forms ionic bonds in organic molecules.

options.label: B
options.text: Nitrogen has an even atomic mass (14 Da) but an odd valence (3 bonds), requiring an odd number of monovalent hydrogens compared to carbon and oxygen.

options.label: C
options.text: Nitrogen contains an unpaired nuclear proton.

options.label: D
options.text: Nitrogen decays radioactively inside the mass spectrometer.

questions.correct_answer: Nitrogen has an even atomic mass (14 Da) but an odd valence (3 bonds), requiring an odd number of monovalent hydrogens compared to carbon and oxygen.
questions.explanation: Because nitrogen forms three bonds with an atomic weight of 14, molecules containing an odd number of nitrogens must contain an odd number of hydrogens.

questions.question: Why does a monochlorinated compound exhibit two molecular ion peaks separated by 2 m/z in a 3:1 intensity ratio?

options.label: A
options.text: The molecule undergoes rapid hydrogen abstraction in the source.

options.label: B
options.text: Chlorine exists naturally as two stable isotopes: ³⁵Cl (75.8% abundance) and ³⁷Cl (24.2% abundance), creating a 3:1 ratio of M⁺ to (M+2)⁺.

options.label: C
options.text: Chlorine fragments into two chloride ions.

options.label: D
options.text: Chlorine absorbs two extra electrons in 25% of molecules.

questions.correct_answer: Chlorine exists naturally as two stable isotopes: ³⁵Cl (75.8% abundance) and ³⁷Cl (24.2% abundance), creating a 3:1 ratio of M⁺ to (M+2)⁺.
questions.explanation: The natural ~3:1 ratio of ³⁵Cl to ³⁷Cl isotopes directly generates the diagnostic M / (M+2) isotopic fingerprint.

questions.topic: Carbonyl IR Force Constant vs Conjugation
questions.question: Why does the C=O stretching frequency decrease from 1715 cm⁻¹ in cyclohexanone to 1685 cm⁻¹ in cyclohex-2-en-1-one?

options.label: A
options.text: Resonance delocalization of π electrons into the adjacent double bond gives the C=O bond more single-bond character, lowering the bond force constant (k).

options.label: B
options.text: Conjugation destroys the carbonyl dipole moment.

options.label: C
options.text: Conjugation increases the reduced mass (μ) of the carbonyl atoms.

options.label: D
options.text: Cyclohexenone undergoes rapid keto-enol tautomerism.

questions.correct_answer: Resonance delocalization of π electrons into the adjacent double bond gives the C=O bond more single-bond character, lowering the bond force constant (k).
questions.explanation: According to Hooke's Law (ν ∝ √(k/μ)), resonance delocalization reduces bond order/force constant k, shifting absorption to lower wavenumber.
